results.summary: Gen 7 finger now traced by colour from the photo, every hole through, three review rounds (7 → 7.5 → 8/10), plus a photo-vs-model compare page
results.detailed_description:
I did all three things you asked: through-holes, a side-by-side comparison page, and a careful pass on the remaining differences. I ran 3 build-and-review rounds; after each one, a separate reviewer agent compared the model with the photos.

Comparison page: https://claude.ai/artifact/SyHvYkvNdHuH3QRGLqouXZ. Pick a round at the top. The first panel draws the model on the photo itself, at the same pixels, and a slider fades between the two. The second panel shows the 3D finger next to the robot, side, top and closed photos, with camera buttons like 'Like the robot photo' and 'Edge-on'. Under that are the changes in each round and what the reviewer found.

The biggest change is the outline. It is no longer clicked by eye. A script picks out the yellow pixels of the finger in the two-hands photo, and every dark spot inside it becomes a hole with its real position and size. So the outline, the steps on the inner edge and all 25 holes now sit where the photo has them.

What changed by round:
• Round 2 (7/10): the colour trace, with every hole cut all the way through.
• Round 3 (7.5/10): smooth edges, blade slots slanted like the photo, a smaller dot, no visible pivot hole.
• Round 4 (8/10): 13 mm thick, wedging down from the black dot to a 4 mm point (the robot and side photos show it), a narrower tip, and a smooth blend where the blade starts.

The reviewer agreed the root honeycomb is right: 8 holes plus 1 small one, the same as the photo.

What still differs, from the final review:
• a crease where the wedge starts at the dot (the photo shows a smooth chamfer);
• slots now a bit too fat;
• one top-left root hole touching the edge;
• three bar holes drawn as ovals that look round in the photo;
• a slightly blunt tip;
• a small kink on the root's outer edge.
I stopped there because you capped it at three rounds.

Things to know:
• The scale is still assumed at 0.2 mm per photo pixel, about 110 mm long. Nothing was measured.
• A few spots where the photo is blurred or covered are drawn by hand: the seam between the two blades, the root corner hidden by the body, and the tip. Each one is listed with its reason in trace_photo.py.
• I removed the placeholder pivot hole because the photo shows that lip solid, so the fingers have no mount at all now.
• Each round's source and renders are saved in rounds/ under the Gen 7 folder. The gallery shows the latest round as Gen 7 after its next refresh.

results.summary: Gen 7 is now just the two yellow fingers, traced point by point from the Generalist two-hands photo
results.detailed_description:
I followed your correction: Gen 7 is not Grabette. It is only the two yellow fingers. There is no body, gears, servo, black carriers, TPU tips or straps.

I traced the outline by hand from the clearest finger in generalist_gripper_gen6_two_hands.png, point by point in pixels, and mapped it to mm. Then I drew the trace back on the photo (previews/overlay.png) to check it lines up. The new finger has the features Gen 6 missed: a wide triangular root with nine bigger pockets, a hooked lip with the carrier slot under it, a slender bar with a staggered honeycomb, two step teeth on the inner edge, a knee where the blade steps outward, and a blade with one black dot and a row of six slanted slots running to a sharp point. Closed, the two points sit 1 mm apart, in the same pose as the photo.

Things to know: the scale is assumed, not measured. I used 0.2 mm per pixel, which gives about 110 mm from pivot to tip; one number (mm_per_px) rescales the whole finger. The 12 mm thickness is a guess from the side photos. With the body deleted, a finger only has a placeholder 3.2 mm pivot hole in the root. The two pivots are 52.6 mm apart because that is where the roots sit in the photo, so the spacing is wider than Gen 6's. Checks pass: the fingers never collide from 0 to 30 degrees, closed tips don't touch, and the meshes are watertight. Gen 7 shows in the gallery with the open/close slider once the 5-minute auto-publish runs.

The registration edits that make it show up as 'Gen 7' (Scripts/publish_designs.py, the Two Finger Gripper README and GENERATIONS.txt) are on disk but not committed, because those files are still untracked in git. That is the same as Gen 6.

Gen 7 = only the two yellow fingers, with no body, mount, camera, straps or drive, matched as closely as possible to the Generalist yellow fingers in cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png (the photos are the source of truth; the best profile views are _two_hands.png, _robot.png and _top.png; use the Insta360 for scale).
